values.name: supplyVoltage
values.why: CITED, not an example: the worked shunt-motor example in Rose-Hulman lecture 25 (research source 419). The picture and every working in the lesson use this set so the writer and the checker agree.
values.realValueLives: research.json source 419 (Rose-Hulman ECE lecture notes 25, slide 25-8). A real motor's own values are on its nameplate.

values.name: armatureResistance
values.why: CITED (source 419): the example's armature resistance. Matches the 0.05 to 0.5 ohm range another source gives for armatures (sources 380, 381).
values.realValueLives: Source 419; on a real motor, the maker's data sheet or a winding-resistance test (source 437 names circuit resistance as a basic check).

values.name: fieldResistance
values.why: CITED (source 419): total shunt-field resistance, so the field current is 600 / 80 = 7.5 A, steady because the field sits across the supply.
values.realValueLives: Source 419; real value on the maker's data sheet or measured with the field leads off and the machine isolated and proved dead.

values.name: ratedLineCurrent
values.why: CITED (source 419): current from the supply at rated load. Armature current = 353 - 7.5 = 345.5 A (computed).
values.realValueLives: Source 419; real value on the nameplate.

values.name: ratedSpeed
values.why: CITED (source 419): rated speed at rated load. The picture's speed scale is relative to this (100 % = 2000 rpm).
values.realValueLives: Source 419; real value on the nameplate.

values.name: ratedBackEmf
values.why: COMPUTED from the cited set by E = V - Ia Ra = 600 - 345.5 x 0.07 = 575.815 V (shown 575.8). The armature drop is 24.2 V, 4.0 % of the supply.
values.realValueLives: Computed on screen from the shown rule E = V - Ia Ra (sources 417, 416).

values.name: noLoadArmatureCurrent
values.why: EXAMPLE, unsourced: the small current that only turns the machine's own friction and iron loss. Label it an example. With it the no-load speed is 2079.8 rpm, so the speed regulation by the NEMA definition (source 406) is (2079.8 - 2000) / 2000 = 4.0 %, which sits just under the 5 to 10 % industry guides give (sources 452, 453). Armature reaction is ignored (flux held constant), said on screen.
values.realValueLives: A no-load test or the maker's data sheet for the real motor; the lesson never states it as a maker's figure.

values.name: speedRedline
values.why: EXAMPLE, unsourced: where the picture's speed bar turns red. Say 'example limit'. A real limit is the 'maximum safe speed' on the nameplate (source 412); a maker also keeps plain straight-shunt stock motors to a field-weakened speed of 105 % of base (source 411).
values.realValueLives: The motor's nameplate maximum safe speed.

values.name: fieldFluxRange
values.unit: % of rated flux (field rheostat 0 to 53.3 ohm)
values.why: EXAMPLE range for the rheostat slider. Flux is taken as proportional to field current (below saturation, said on screen), so flux fraction f = 80 / (80 + Rc). Load TORQUE is held constant while the field is weakened, so Ia = 345.5 / f and speed = 2000 x (E / 575.8) / f. Computed table: f 1.0 -> 2000 rpm; 0.9 -> 2212 (Rc 8.9 ohm); 0.8 -> 2474 (Rc 20.0 ohm, just past the example redline); 0.7 -> 2806 (Rc 34.3 ohm); 0.6 -> 3240 rpm (Rc 53.3 ohm, Ia 575.8 A).
values.realValueLives: A real machine's field curve (flux against field current) from the maker; real limits are on the nameplate (source 412).

values.name: openFieldResidualFlux
values.why: EXAMPLE, unsourced: the weak flux left by residual magnetism when the field opens. Used only to drive the animation; the picture prints NO speed number, it runs the bar off the scale into red and says 'runs away on a light load' (sources 420, 422). Where a load is on the shaft, the lesson says the speed depends on the load (contested note: source 423 says it may keep running on residual magnetism).
values.realValueLives: Not a design figure; depends on the iron and its history. Never state a number for a real motor.

values.name: startingCurrentLimit
values.why: EXAMPLE CHOICE inside the cited range: starting resistors limit the starting current to 125 to 200 percent of full-load current (source 442). Direct on the 600 V supply the armature would take 600 / 0.07 = 8571 A, 24.8 times rated (computed; compare source 441: 650 A, about twelve times, for its 10 hp example). A 150 % limit needs total resistance 600 / 518.3 = 1.158 ohm, so about 1.09 ohm external. These are computed from the example set, not from any starter data sheet.
values.realValueLives: The starter maker's data sheet and the motor's rated current.

values.name: irDropBarMagnification
values.why: DISPLAY CHOICE: at true scale the armature-drop bar (24 V of 600 V) is too thin to see, so the picture draws it 10 times larger and says so beside the bar. Never presented as the real proportion.
values.realValueLives: True scale is 4.0 % of the supply at rated load (computed).

values.name: speedRegulationTaught
values.value: a few percent, about 4 % in the picture; 5 to 10 % in industry guides; his sheet says 10 to 20 %
values.why: The lesson teaches the range as contested (research.json i7 notes): the NEMA definition (source 406) is the rule; the picture's 4.0 % is computed from the cited set and the example no-load current. IDC's '7 to 10 %' belongs to Ward-Leonard control, not a plain shunt motor, so it is not used as a shunt figure (note added in research.reply.txt).
values.realValueLives: The real motor's data sheet or a no-load against full-load test.
